decisions.reason: The carrier wafer is a low-cost option closely related to existing capabilities, so while its niche demand remains uncertain, the firm can keep the option open without significant resource drain.

Because it is a flagship focus aligned with the firm's packaging-wafer direction and benefits from existing material capabilities, the copper interposer retains option value despite unresolved technical and demand uncertainty.
The off-the-shelf brand is close to the established offer and maintains multiple models at low incremental cost, so its option value is high and the likelihood of withdrawal is low.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the firm's established capabilities and require costly new resources without evidence of traction, so the option is no longer worth keeping open relative to its cost.
